# Lagrangian Optimization and KKT Conditions

Constrained optimisation underpins SVMs, variational inference, and safe RL. The Lagrangian converts constraints into penalties; KKT conditions characterise constrained optima.

## Equality Constraints: Lagrange Multipliers

min f(x) s.t. gᵢ(x) = 0. Lagrangian: L(x,λ) = f(x) + Σλᵢgᵢ(x). Stationarity: ∇f + Σλᵢ∇gᵢ = 0. Interpretation: at optimum, ∇f lies in the span of constraint gradients.

## KKT Conditions for Inequality Constraints

| Condition | Formula | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| Stationarity | ∇_x L = 0 | Lagrangian gradient vanishes |
| Primal feasibility | g(x)≤0, h(x)=0 | Constraints satisfied |
| Dual feasibility | μ ≥ 0 | Inequality multipliers non-negative |
| Complementary slackness | μᵢgᵢ(x)=0 | Active constraints have non-zero multiplier |

## Duality and Strong Duality

Dual: d(μ,λ) = inf_x L(x,μ,λ) ≤ f* (weak duality always). Strong duality (d*=f*): guaranteed by Slater's condition for convex problems (strictly feasible interior point).

## SVM Dual

w* = Σαᵢyᵢxᵢ. Dual: max Σαᵢ − ½ΣᵢΣⱼ αᵢαⱼyᵢyⱼ K(xᵢ,xⱼ). Support vectors: αᵢ > 0 by complementary slackness. Kernel trick: replace xᵢᵀxⱼ with K(xᵢ,xⱼ).

## Constrained RL (Primal-Dual)

max E[Σrₜ] s.t. E[Σcₜ] ≤ d. Lagrangian L(π,λ) = E_π[Σrₜ] − λ(E_π[Σcₜ]−d). Alternate: policy gradient on reward−λ·cost; gradient ascent on λ. λ is shadow price of the safety constraint.

## Variational Inference Connection

ELBO = log p(x) − KL(q‖p). β-VAE adds Lagrange multiplier β on the KL term, enforcing disentanglement by tightening the prior constraint.
